title: Spirometry with bronchodilator
what: You breathe out hard into a tube, then inhale a medicine that opens the airways, and breathe out again. This shows if your breathing improves with the medicine.
why: For cough, shortness of breath, or wheezing, to check for asthma and COPD, or to track treatment.
duration: usually 30 to 40 minutes; the report is often ready right away or the same day
tell_doctor: What inhalers and breathing medicines you use
If you recently had eye, chest, or belly surgery
If you recently had a heart attack or have heart disease
If you have a cold or a flare-up right now

prepare.title: Inhalers
prepare.text: Some inhalers are not used for several hours before the test. Do not stop them on your own. Ask your doctor in advance.

prepare.title: Smoking and coffee
prepare.text: Do not smoke for at least a few hours before the test. No coffee or strong tea in the morning.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light breakfast, nothing heavy for 2 hours before. No hard exercise before the test.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Loose clothes, with no tight belt.

steps: You sit, and a clip is put on your nose
You seal your lips tightly around the tube
You take a deep breath in and breathe out as hard and as long as you can
You repeat this 3 times or more
You inhale the medicine from an inhaler
After 15 to 20 minutes, you repeat the breaths out
feel: The repeated breaths may make you dizzy or want to cough
The medicine can cause slight shaking or a fast heartbeat. It passes
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
Use your own inhalers as usual, unless your doctor said otherwise
The report is often ready right away

faq.q: Why the medicine during the test?
faq.a: If breathing clearly improves after it, this helps the doctor understand the illness and how to treat it.

faq.q: Can I use my inhaler in the morning?
faq.a: Do not decide on your own. Ask your doctor in advance. Some inhalers should not be used before the test.

reminders.text: Spirometry with bronchodilator tomorrow. Ask your doctor about your inhalers. No smoking or coffee in the morning.
